results: 1. Bedside examination of extraocular movements, including assessment for ptosis and pupil reactivity to light
cranial nerve examination: partial right oculomotor palsy with right adduction failure, mild vertical gaze limitation, mildly impaired convergence, and partial ptosis; pupils equally reactive
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
subjective visual vertical: within normal limits
head impulse test: normal - no corrective saccade
pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
3. MRI of the brain with attention to the midbrain and cavernous sinus
MRI brain with gadolinium: small dorsal paramedian midbrain infarct
MRI sella and orbits: normal pituitary and orbits
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute dorsal paramedian midbrain infarction causing a pupil-sparing partial oculomotor nerve palsy
Alternative 1: Cavernous sinus pathology (e.g., aneurysm or tumor) compressing the third cranial nerve
Alternative 2: Microvascular ischemic oculomotor neuropathy
